newsitem.title: USA: Productivity a key to US social security--Broaddus.
newsitem.headline: Productivity a key to US social security--Broaddus.

text.p: Richmond Federal Reserve Bank President Alfred Broaddus on Friday said a key to saving social security lies in increasing U.S. productivity.

In remarks to a teacher group at the University of South Carolina, Broaddus said that "economics can help in this situation, economics makes it clear that the only real way out of this box is through greater productivity."
He said this will require a larger capital stock and the way to get this was to consume less and save more.
He told the group that the most effective action the Fed could take to help the U.S. economy was to rid it of inflation once and for all.

"Further, my experience, my work and my studies have also led me to the conclusion that the rate of inflation...is the only economic variable the Fed in its conduct of monetary policy can decisively control and influence over time," he said.
